vroot — plain-text reference for agents
Version 2.2.x · MIT · https://github.com/gairxx/vroot
This file is self-contained. It is the same information the website shows,
without JavaScript, HTML chrome or navigation.

===============================================================================
1. WHAT VROOT IS
===============================================================================

vroot is one Bash script. It turns a flag into an isolated Linux root shell:

    vroot -python          a root shell with Python
    vroot -node -python    a shell with Node and Python merged
    vroot -rust -- cargo build   run a command instead of a shell

It is not Docker: there is no daemon and no image build queue. A flag set maps
to one or more "recipes"; recipes are merged into a single-file squashfs image
(`<flags>-<10-hex>.sqfs`) built once and cached. Each session unpacks the image
to a cache directory and runs it through bubblewrap with overlayfs, so you get
uid 0 with full capabilities inside the sandbox, but confined by user, PID,
mount, UTS and IPC namespaces. The host filesystem is not visible unless you
bind it explicitly with -v.

Design goals that matter to agents:
  - No sudo, no daemon, no service to start.
  - Deterministic, content-addressed env images.
  - Machine-readable output (--json) on stdout, diagnostics on stderr.
  - Safe under concurrency: parallel builds of the same env serialise.
  - Snapshots are single files you can copy, hand off, or boot elsewhere.

===============================================================================
2. REQUIREMENTS AND INSTALL
===============================================================================

Host: Linux with unprivileged user namespaces.
Required: bubblewrap, util-linux (unshare), squashfs-tools (mksquashfs,
unsquashfs), curl (or wget).
Optional: docker — only for flags whose recipe targets the Debian base
(bun, clojure, groovy, julia, kotlin, scala, swift).

Install (no sudo):

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gairxx/vroot/main/install.sh | sh

Options: --prefix DIR (default $HOME/.local), --version REF (default main),
--uninstall, -h.

Or run in place:

    git clone https://github.com/gairxx/vroot && bash vroot/vroot -python

Check the host:

    vroot doctor

Storage root: $VROOT_HOME (default ~/.local/share/vroot)
Recipes dir:  $VROOT_CONFIG/recipes (default ~/.config/vroot/recipes)

===============================================================================
3. CLI SYNOPSIS
===============================================================================

    vroot [FLAGS] [NAME] [OPTIONS] [-- COMMAND]

  - FLAGS    one per tool/language, e.g. -python, -node. Combine freely.
  - NAME     a sandbox name; makes the sandbox persistent and reusable.
  - -- CMD   run CMD and exit instead of opening an interactive shell.
  - A bare `vroot` prints a quick-start banner; it does NOT open a shell.
    Use `vroot -base` for a blank Alpine root shell.

Examples:

    vroot -base                     blank Alpine root shell
    vroot -python                   root shell with Python
    vroot -php -sqlite -git         compose tools
    vroot -python work              persistent sandbox named "work"
    vroot work -- python3 -V        reuse it, run one command
    vroot -go -v ~/src:/src -- ls /src   expose a host dir (rw)
    vroot -python -offline          no network
    vroot -node -- node -e 'console.log(process.version)'

===============================================================================
4. OPTIONS
===============================================================================

  -v SRC[:DST][:ro]   expose a host path (default: nothing from the host)
  -offline / -o       no network (loopback only)
  -net                re-enable network (default)
  -cwd DIR            working directory (default /root)
  -env K=V            set an environment variable (repeatable)
  -name NAME          persistent sandbox name
  -hostname H         hostname inside (default: the sandbox name)
  -clean              start with an empty environment
  -rm                 delete the sandbox after this session
  -json / --json      machine-readable output
  -h / --help         help

===============================================================================
5. FLAGS (42)
===============================================================================

Column order: flag, base, aliases, description. Aliases are `provides` entries,
so -python3 and -py resolve to the same environment as -python.

  -base       alpine  alpine                                 Bare Alpine root shell (default)
  -bun        debian  -                                      Bun runtime (installed from bun.sh)
  -clang      alpine  llvm                                   Clang / LLVM C and C++ toolchain
  -clojure    debian  clj, cljs                              Clojure (Debian package)
  -cmake      alpine  -                                      CMake build system
  -crystal    alpine  shards                                 Crystal language
  -curl       alpine  wget, http                             curl and wget with CA certs
  -d          alpine  dmd, ldc, dlang                        D language (LDC + dub)
  -debian     debian  deb                                    Bare Debian root shell (glibc)
  -deno       alpine  typescript, ts                         Deno (with built-in TypeScript)
  -dotnet     alpine  .net, dotnet8, csharp, c#              .NET 8 SDK (C#, F#, VB)
  -elixir     alpine  mix, iex                               Elixir on Erlang/OTP
  -erlang     alpine  erl, escript                           Erlang/OTP
  -fsharp     alpine  f#, fsc                                F# on the .NET 8 SDK
  -gcc        alpine  cc, g++                                GCC C and C++ toolchain
  -gfortran   alpine  fortran                                GNU Fortran compiler
  -git        alpine  gh                                     Git with SSH client
  -go         alpine  golang                                 Go toolchain
  -groovy     debian  -                                      Apache Groovy (Debian package)
  -haskell    alpine  ghc, cabal, stack                      GHC and Cabal
  -java       alpine  jdk, jre, javac                        OpenJDK 17
  -julia      debian  -                                      Julia (installed from julialang.org)
  -kotlin     debian  kotlinc                                Kotlin compiler (from JetBrains releases)
  -lua        alpine  lua5, lua5.4, luajit                   Lua 5.4 with LuaRocks
  -mysql      alpine  mariadb                                MariaDB server and client
  -nasm       alpine  asm                                    NASM assembler
  -nim        alpine  nimble                                 Nim compiler
  -node       alpine  nodejs, npm, javascript, js            Node.js and npm
  -ocaml      alpine  opam, dune                             OCaml with opam and dune
  -openssh    alpine  ssh, sshd                              OpenSSH client and server
  -perl       alpine  cpan                                   Perl
  -php        alpine  php8                                   PHP 8.3 with common extensions
  -postgres   alpine  postgresql, psql                       PostgreSQL server and client
  -python     alpine  python3, py                            Python 3 with pip
  -r          alpine  rlang, rscript                         R statistical language
  -ruby       alpine  gem, irb                               Ruby with RubyGems
  -rust       alpine  cargo, rustc                           Rust compiler and Cargo
  -scala      debian  scala3                                 Scala 3 (from scala-lang releases)
  -sqlite     alpine  sqlite3                                SQLite CLI
  -swift      debian  -                                      Swift toolchain (from swift.org)
  -vim        alpine  vi, editor                             Vim and Neovim
  -zig        alpine  -                                      Zig compiler

===============================================================================
6. MANAGEMENT COMMANDS
===============================================================================

  vroot build FLAGS...        build (or reuse) an env image; prints its path
  vroot ls | list             list sandboxes
  vroot rm NAME... | --all    delete sandboxes
  vroot info NAME             sandbox details
  vroot save NAME [OUT.vroot] pack a sandbox (with changes) into one image
  vroot OUT.vroot             boot from a saved image file
  vroot envs | images         list built env images and cached bases
  vroot prune | gc            clear caches and temporary files
  vroot filetype [install|uninstall|status]
                              register .vroot/*.sqfs as a file type
  vroot recipe list|show NAME|new NAME|edit NAME|path
                              browse or author recipes
  vroot doctor                check the host setup
  vroot help                  full help
  vroot version               print version

===============================================================================
7. JSON INTERFACE
===============================================================================

JSON is written to stdout, exactly one value per invocation, always newline
terminated. Logs and warnings go to stderr. `-json` and `--json` are
equivalent.

  vroot build -python --json
      {"env":"/home/u/.local/share/vroot/envs/python-84d0423ed3.sqfs","cached":false}
      Keys: env (absolute path), cached (bool: true if the image already existed).

  vroot ls --json
      [{"name":"work","env":"python-84d0423ed3.sqfs",
        "image":"/…/python-84d0423ed3.sqfs","bytes":123456,"age_minutes":12}]
      One object per sandbox. age_minutes is null when the creation time is
      unknown or unparsable.

  vroot envs --json
      {"images":[{"file":"python-84d0423ed3.sqfs","bytes":26214400}],
       "bases":[{"name":"alpine","bytes":8123456}]}
      images = env squashfs files; bases = unpacked base rootfs cache.

  vroot info NAME --json
      {"name":"work","env":"python-84d0423ed3.sqfs","image":"/…/python.sqfs",
       "created":"2026-10-31T12:00:00+00:00","bytes":4096,
       "changed_files":3,"path":"/…/instances/work"}
      changed_files counts entries in the sandbox's upper (writable) layer.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    error (unknown flag, missing sandbox, build failure, bad arguments)
  N    with `-- CMD`, vroot forwards the command's own exit status (e.g. 42)

===============================================================================
8. CONCURRENCY AND ATOMICITY
===============================================================================

Several agents may hit the same env at once. vroot is built for that:

  - Build lock: building an env takes a directory lock at
    "<envfile>.lock" (mkdir). A second builder waits up to ~180 s for the
    image to appear instead of racing mksquashfs on the same path.
  - Atomic cache unpack: the image is unpacked into "<cache>.tmp.$$" and then
    swapped in with rm -rf + mv, so no process sees a half-written tree.
  - Content-addressed names: the image name embeds a 10-hex sha256 of the
    resolved recipe contents plus the base, so identical inputs reuse one file.
  - Distinct envs build and run independently; there is no global lock.

===============================================================================
9. PERSISTENCE, SNAPSHOTS AND FORKS
===============================================================================

Named sandbox:   vroot -python work
  Changes go to instances/work/upper (overlayfs upper layer). Reusing the name
  reattaches the same env; using a different env with the same name is an error.

Snapshot:        vroot save work out.vroot
  Packs the merged filesystem (env + your changes) into one squashfs file with
  a .vroot extension. Boot it anywhere vroot is installed:
      vroot out.vroot -- cat /root/notes.txt

Fork: name a sandbox from an image, or copy a saved image and boot it under a
  new name. Because images are immutable single files, copies are independent
  checkpoints: launch two sandboxes from the same image and their writes never
  intersect.

===============================================================================
10. ISOLATION MODEL
===============================================================================

Inside the sandbox you are uid 0 with CAP_ALL, but:
  - user namespace (unprivileged), mapped to your host user
  - separate PID, UTS, IPC (and best-effort cgroup) namespaces
  - the root filesystem is an overlayfs mount: lower = cached env image
    (read-only), upper = tmpfs (ephemeral) or the named sandbox's upper/ dir
  - /proc, /dev, /tmp, /run are fresh; /sys is read-only if present
  - no host paths are visible unless bound with -v
  - -offline removes the network namespace

Nothing runs as root on the host, and no host file is written except under
$VROOT_HOME (envs, cache, instances, tmp, recipe-index).

===============================================================================
11. STORAGE LAYOUT
===============================================================================

$VROOT_HOME/
  envs/<slug>-<hash>.sqfs    built env images (content-addressed)
  cache/<slug>-<hash>/       unpacked, read-only lower layer
  cache/.bases/<base>/       unpacked base rootfs cache
  instances/<name>/          persistent sandboxes
      meta                   ENV=…, IMG=…, CREATED=…
      upper/ work/ .merged/  overlayfs layers
  tmp/                       scratch; run roots for ephemeral sandboxes
  recipe-index/              flag → recipe index (one file per flag) + .stamp

===============================================================================
12. RECIPE FORMAT
===============================================================================

A recipe is a key = value file in recipes/ (built in) or
$VROOT_CONFIG/recipes/ (yours). Minimal example:

    name        = python
    provides    = python,python3,py
    base        = alpine
    packages    = python3 py3-pip
    setup       = ln -sf /usr/bin/python3 /usr/local/bin/python
    env         = PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    path        = /usr/local/bin
    verify      = python3 --version
    description = Python 3 interpreter and pip

Keys:
  name         canonical recipe name (defaults to the filename)
  provides     comma/space list of flags and aliases that select this recipe
  base         alpine (default) or debian (needs docker on the host)
  packages     packages passed to apk add / apt-get install (repeatable)
  setup        shell lines run at build time (repeatable)
  env          KEY=VAL lines exported in every sandbox (repeatable)
  path         extra PATH entries, prepended
  verify       commands run at the end of the build (repeatable)
  description  one-line human summary (shown by `vroot recipe list`)
  docs         documentation URL

Resolution precedence (do not rely on anything else):
  1. a user recipe whose filename matches the flag
  2. a user recipe whose `provides` contains the flag
  3. a built-in recipe whose filename matches the flag
  4. a built-in recipe whose `provides` contains the flag

Add a recipe:

    vroot recipe new mytool     # creates ~/.config/vroot/recipes/mytool.conf
    vroot recipe edit mytool
    vroot recipe list           # see it in the catalogue
    vroot -mytool               # use it

===============================================================================
13. RULES FOR AGENTS
===============================================================================

  1. Prefer `vroot build FLAGS --json` to obtain an env path; parse stdout as
     JSON and treat stderr as logs, not data.
  2. Use `-- CMD` for one-shot work; it forwards the command's exit status.
  3. Name sandboxes for state that must survive; use unnamed ephemeral runs for
     everything else (they leave nothing behind).
  4. Use `vroot save NAME out.vroot` for a checkpoint, and boot the file to
     fork independent copies.
  5. Check exit codes, not stderr text; errors are one `err …` line, exit 1.
  6. Run `vroot doctor` once per host before assuming failure is your bug.
  7. Never assume the host filesystem is visible: bind explicitly with -v.
